sources: Full text: PMC7244552 (Nat Commun 11:2590), '16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing'
Supplementary Table 6 (41467_2020_16224_MOESM1_ESM.pdf p.11): the exact primer sequences
Source data Fig4B_data.xlsx (41467_2020_16224_MOESM3_ESM.zip): the mouse -> diet / cage / site key

amplicon.paper_statement: The V4 region was amplified with barcoded universal primers 'modified from the standard 515F-806R primers to reduce host mitochondrial rRNA gene amplification'. Supplementary Table 6 lists the pair as 519F-806R. Sequenced by Fulgent Genetics on MiSeq, 2 x 300 bp.
amplicon.primer_evidence: The paper's own primers were checked against the reads and are absent (0% of R1 and R2 over 3 runs x 3000 reads). The reads begin at TACGTAGGTG etc., i.e. the 16S sequence immediately 3' of 519F, so the libraries reached ENA already primer-trimmed. Therefore trimLeft = 0: trimming the stated primer lengths again would cut 15 and 20 bp of real sequence.

insert_length_primer_free.method: measured two independent ways that agree: 83.4% of R1 reads run through into revcomp(806R), and R1 vs revcomp(R2) overlap alignment over 2412 pairs
insert_length_primer_free.note: Essentially a fixed-length amplicon (the classic 253 bp V4), unlike V3-V4 or V1-V3. The 0.5% tail out to ~420 bp in the overlap probe is mis-aligned junk, not a real second mode.

amplicon.trunc_len_basis: RAW read coordinates (truncLen applies before trimLeft, and trimLeft is 0 here, so truncLen is the retained biological length directly).
amplicon.read_through: SEVERE and must be handled: the reads are 301 bp but the insert is 253 bp, so 83% of reads run past the far end into the reverse primer and adaptor. truncLen MUST be <= 253 on both mates. Truncating at the read length would denoise adaptor sequence as if it were 16S.
amplicon.max_trunc_len_reason: capped at the insert length: beyond it the read is adaptor, not 16S

technical_controls_in_run_set.rule: aliases beginning Buffer_, GF_ or CC_SW_Chow_ are NOT mouse gut samples and must be excluded from any abundance matrix
technical_controls_in_run_set.what_they_are: Buffer_* extraction blanks; GF_* germ-free small-intestine and stool negative controls; CC_SW_Chow_* a cecal-contents dilution series and sequencing replicates used to establish the limits of quantification
technical_controls_in_run_set.keep_them_for: contaminant identification and limit-of-quantification checks, as their own table

alias_decoder.P_vs_NP: the two cage-mates within one cage; what P/NP abbreviates is not stated in the paper and is NOT needed for the group assignment, so it is left unexpanded rather than guessed
alias_decoder.evidence: the Source/Site columns of Fig4B_data.xlsx give these expansions verbatim

group_assignment.evidence: The Diet column of Fig4B_data.xlsx assigns Keto to M1-M3 and Control to M4-M6, for both the P and NP cage-mate. That gives 6 ketogenic and 6 control mice, matching the paper's 'split into two groups (n = 6 each)'.
group_assignment.caution: The group follows the MOUSE NUMBER, not the P/NP suffix. Cage is fully confounded with diet (cage n holds mouse n's pair), so cage cannot be used as a covariate.
group_assignment.design_note: Day 0 stool was taken BEFORE the diets were introduced, so D0 samples are baseline for both arms, not yet keto.

not_usable_for: absolute abundance: the dPCR anchor is in the paper's source data, not the FASTQs
cage as a covariate: cage is confounded with diet

experiment.host: Mus musculus (Swiss Webster, 4 weeks old at diet start)
experiment.body_site: GI tract: stool plus lumenal contents and mucosa from stomach, upper/lower small intestine, cecum and colon
experiment.design: ketogenic diet vs vitamin/mineral-matched control diet, n = 6 mice each; stool at days 0/4/7/10, all other sites at day 10 necropsy
experiment.note: The paper's own quantification is ABSOLUTE abundance (16S copies by dPCR x relative abundance). Re-deriving relative abundance from the reads reproduces only the relative half; the dPCR anchor is in the paper's source data, not in the FASTQs.
